summary.headline: The Planning Board reviewed the proposed two-family zoning bylaw, continued several hearings, and reviewed Fay School landscape mitigation plans.
summary.summary: At its remote meeting, the Planning Board held a public hearing on the Zoning Board of Appeals-sponsored two-family dwelling zoning bylaw amendment, discussing definitions and lot requirements before voting to continue the hearing to September 28. The board also voted to continue hearings for site plan modifications at 154 Turnpike Road and 22 Turnpike Road. In other business, representatives from Fay School presented their landscape sustainability plan to satisfy conditions for their building addition, and the board heard updates on the upcoming Costco application.

topics.title: Public hearing on two-family dwelling zoning bylaw amendment
topics.summary: The board opened a public hearing on a proposed zoning bylaw amendment sponsored by the Zoning Board of Appeals to add a definition for two-family dwellings and regulate conversions and new construction by special permit. Board members and staff discussed removing specific examples like duplex and townhouse from the definition to avoid confusion, and addressed how accessory dwelling units and zoning district lot size rules interact with two-family housing. The board decided to continue the public hearing rather than take a final position before the warrant is signed.
key_details: Sponsored by the Zoning Board of Appeals to remove an existing two-year waiting period for single-family conversions and define two-family dwellings.
Discussion centered on clarifying definitions to ensure ADUs are not categorized as three-family dwellings.
Board members favored striking parenthetical references to townhouse and duplex from the proposed text.
Select Board is scheduled to sign the Special Town Meeting warrant the following day.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to September 28, 2026 at 6:30 PM.
topics.why_it_matters: Changes to zoning bylaws govern what types of housing can be built or converted across Southborough neighborhoods and will go before voters at Town Meeting.

topics.title: 154 Turnpike Road major site plan modification
topics.summary: Capital Group Properties requested a continuation of the public hearing regarding non-compliance modifications to their major site plan concerning landscaping and lighting. The applicant is installing dimmer switches to meet lighting calculations, which board members will inspect during an evening site visit before the next meeting.
key_details: 154 Turnpike Road involves non-compliance modifications regarding landscaping and site lighting.
Applicant submitted updated cut sheets for gooseneck sign fixtures and plans to install lighting dimmers.
A board member will conduct a night visit to confirm dimmer installation prior to the next hearing.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to September 28, 2026 at 6:45 PM.

topics.title: 22 Turnpike Road golf range site plan modification
topics.summary: The applicant for 22 Turnpike Road requested a continuation of the hearing and an extension of the board's decision deadline for a major site plan modification. A third submission of materials has been forwarded to Nitsch Engineering for follow-up peer review.
key_details: Project involves site plan modifications for the golf range at 22 Turnpike Road.
Nitsch Engineering is conducting follow-up peer review on submission number three.
Applicant requested extending the decision deadline to October 23, 2026.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to September 28, 2026 at 6:45 PM; decision deadline extended to October 23, 2026.

topics.title: Planning Board goals and Master Plan 2030 planning
topics.summary: The board reviewed a draft list of 2026 goals and discussed planning for the 2030 Master Plan update. Members and staff discussed forming a new Master Plan Committee and exploring a hybrid approach with a consultant, which may require seeking grant funding or a Town Meeting warrant article for roughly $70,000 to $100,000.
key_details: Master Plan Implementation Committee is developing the approach for the upcoming 2030 Master Plan update.
Estimated consultant costs are approximately $70,000 to $100,000.
Full board discussion and formal goal adoption postponed until the board chair returns.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; item to return when the full board is present.

topics.title: Subdivision rules and regulations update
topics.summary: Board member Alan Beliak reported on progress rewriting the town's subdivision rules and regulations. A new document structure is being tested, and the working group plans to consult Town Counsel regarding the opening definitions section.
key_details: Working group tested a restructured approach to the regulations document.
Next step is consulting Town Counsel on legal definitions.

topics.title: Zoning enforcement and interdepartmental coordination
topics.summary: The town planner reported on monthly collaborative meetings with the building commissioner to review outstanding site plan conditions and track non-compliant projects. Staff is compiling a comprehensive spreadsheet to track required follow-ups before building permits and occupancy certificates are issued.
key_details: Monthly coordination meetings between planning staff and the building commissioner began in September.
Staff is developing a tracking spreadsheet of non-compliant conditions and outstanding permits.

topics.title: Fay School building addition landscape mitigation plan
topics.summary: Representatives from Fay School presented an 18-page sustainability and landscape plan required as part of conditions for their temporary certificate of occupancy. Because some non-native cultivars were planted instead of approved native species and three trees were removed during construction, Fay School proposed replanting replacement native trees and integrating pollinator plantings and student curriculum initiatives.
key_details: Fay School plans to plant two Silver Maples, one Serviceberry, and replacement native trees across campus to mitigate past tree removals.
One Eastern Redbud has already been planted.
Fuss and O'Neill is concluding peer review of the project's as-built drawings.
Planning staff will provide a formal notice of conditions to Fay School to finalize an enforceable agreement before granting a full certificate of occupancy.
topics.outcome: Town planner to send formal conditions list; Fay School will update and sign commitment document.

topics.title: Town planner's report and project updates
topics.summary: The town planner reviewed multiple administrative and development updates. Costco submitted major site plan and special permit applications with an 88-page plan set scheduled to open for public hearing on September 28. Staff also reported on the FY28 budget timeline, the state's upcoming ADU regulation revisions, and Attorney General approval of the 2026 Annual Town Meeting bylaws with a noted scrivener's error regarding battery energy storage systems in the Industrial Park district.
key_details: Costco applications for major site plan, highway retail special permit, and lower impact development special permit will open for hearing on September 28.
Nitsch Engineering is revising its scope and fee for traffic peer review on the Costco project.
Planning Board FY28 budget submissions are due to the Select Board by October 13, 2026; Marnie Houlihan was appointed budget liaison.
Attorney General approved Annual Town Meeting bylaws, noting a cross-reference error regarding battery energy storage systems in the IP district.
Town is preparing for the 2027 Tercentennial celebration and pursuing grant funding for Fayville Park expansion parking.
topics.outcome: Informational report presented; Marnie Houlihan designated as Planning Board budget liaison.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing on the proposed two-family dwelling zoning bylaw amendment to September 28, 2026 at 6:30 PM.
Continue the public hearing for 154 Turnpike Road major site plan approval modification to September 28, 2026 at 6:45 PM.
Continue the public hearing for 22 Turnpike Road major site plan approval modification to September 28, 2026 at 6:45 PM.
Extend the decision due date for 22 Turnpike Road major site plan approval modification by 60 days to October 23, 2026.

public_comment.summary: A former Planning Board chair asked why each zoning district section in the proposed two-family bylaw repeated language requiring lots to meet the minimum lot size for the district, warning it creates ambiguity given that some commercial districts have smaller lot minimums than residential zones.
